_note: Approved/limited_use snapshot only. Not the full research dataset. A phrase here is a candidate to consider when it fits the exact meaning, platform, audience and register of the copy you're writing — never insert it just because it's listed.

phrases.english_concept: the head term for the whole product category in the Indian market
phrases.usage_guidance: Already the anchor of the hi/ pages ('स्टाइलिश नाम जनरेटर', 'फ्री फायर स्टाइलिश नाम') — that instinct is right and is confirmed by the whole competitive field. Keep it as the primary head term for hi/. Note that a large share of Indian users type the query in Latin ('stylish naam', 'stylish name'), so the Devanagari title should sit alongside Latin-script mentions of the same term in the page's own copy, which the existing hi/ pages already do by mixing scripts.
phrases.good_example: स्टाइलिश नाम जनरेटर — फैंसी नाम और निकनेम, सीधे कॉपी करें।
phrases.avoid_when: Do not substitute a 'purer' Hindi rendering in a title. 'सुंदर नाम' or 'आकर्षक नाम' would be correct Hindi and commercially invisible.

phrases.native_phrase: गिल्ड नेम / स्क्वाड / सिंबल्स / फॉन्ट (not संघ / दल / प्रतीक / लिपि)
phrases.english_concept: the Hinglish code-switch rule — in gaming/social compounds, Hindi uses the transliterated English noun, not the native Hindi one
phrases.register: neutral-casual for the target audience; would read wrong in formal/government Hindi
phrases.content_surface: title/H1/meta, h2_h3, body, faq, tool copy — a rule over all of them
phrases.usage_guidance: Standing rule for hi/: when a technology or gaming concept has an English name, transliterate it (फॉन्ट, सिंबल, कॉपी, पेस्ट, बायो, प्रोफाइल, गिल्ड, क्लैन, निकनेम). Reserve native Hindi vocabulary for the connective and explanatory tissue. The live hi/ pages already do this well (e.g. 'Discord टेक्स्ट फॉर्मेटिंग समझें', 'फैंसी फॉन्ट कॉपी पेस्ट') — this row exists to make it a documented rule rather than an accident, and to stop a future translator 'purifying' it.
phrases.good_example: अपने गिल्ड नेम में स्टाइलिश फॉन्ट और यूनिक सिंबल्स इस्तेमाल करें।
phrases.avoid_when: Formal, legal, accessibility or policy copy should shift toward standard Hindi. And never mix the two registers inside one sentence for no reason.

phrases.english_concept: the team/clan unit — Free Fire's India-market term is 'guild', not 'clan'
phrases.usage_guidance: On hi/usecase/free-fire-naam-stylish/, use 'गिल्ड नेम' for the team-name section; on hi/usecase/pubg-bgmi-naam-stylish/, use 'क्लैन'. Match the game's own label, per game. The cost-in-diamonds fact is good FAQ material because it explains why users want to get the name right first time — the same argument the site's name-length checker already serves.
phrases.good_example: गिल्ड नेम छोटा और याद रखने में आसान रखें — बदलने पर 500 डायमंड लगते हैं।
phrases.avoid_when: Do not use 'गिल्ड' on BGMI/PUBG pages, and do not use it as a general word for a gaming team outside Free Fire.

phrases.english_concept: what a 'stylish name' actually is when the input is Devanagari — the letters do not change, only the frame does
phrases.register: neutral; the underlying examples are gaming-informal
phrases.usage_guidance: Two consequences, both wording-level (this is not a build brief): (1) hi/ copy should set the expectation honestly — Devanagari letters stay as they are, the styling comes from frames and symbols — rather than implying 100+ fonts apply to Hindi text. (2) hi/ pages should foreground the decoration/frame tabs over the font grid, and should show worked Devanagari examples framed the way Indian players actually write them. An honest 'हिंदी अक्षर वैसे ही रहते हैं, स्टाइल फ्रेम और सिंबल से आता है' is a genuine differentiator, because the machine-translated competition does not say it.
phrases.good_example: हिंदी में नाम लिखें और उसे ꧁༒…༒꧂ जैसे फ्रेम में सजाएँ — अक्षर वही रहते हैं, लुक बदल जाता है।
phrases.avoid_when: Do not claim Devanagari can be converted to bold/cursive/gothic Unicode. Do not present the Latin font grid as the answer to a Devanagari input.

phrases.native_phrase: एटीट्यूड नाम / भक्ति नाम (महाकाल) / देसी नाम
phrases.transliteration: attitude naam / bhakti naam / desi naam
phrases.english_concept: the Indian name-category taxonomy — attitude, VIP, bhakti/Mahakal, desi
phrases.register: informal, youth; 'भक्ति/महाकाल' is culturally loaded and sincere, not ironic
phrases.content_surface: h2_h3, body, generator example copy, ready-made-name list groupings
phrases.usage_guidance: If hi/ pages carry ready-made-name lists or generator themes, these are the categories Indian users expect to see, and using them is a strong native signal. Treat 'attitude' as the default high-volume grouping.
phrases.good_example: एटीट्यूड नाम, गेमिंग नाम और भक्ति नाम — अपनी पसंद की कैटेगरी चुनें।
phrases.avoid_when: **Handle the devotional category with care.** Religious names (महाकाल, महादेव, भोलेनाथ) are sincere identity markers, not decoration — never treat them as a novelty, never pair them with skull/violence ornaments as if interchangeable, and never auto-generate them by random recombination. If in doubt, offer them as a curated list rather than generative output. Also keep 'attitude' out of guide/answers-style explanatory copy.

phrases.native_phrase: बहुत लंबा नाम / बहुत ज्यादा सिंबल्स डाल देना जिससे पढ़ना मुश्किल हो
phrases.transliteration: bahut lamba naam / bahut zyada symbols
phrases.english_concept: the two named user complaints about decorated names — too long, and too many symbols to read
phrases.usage_guidance: Use as FAQ headings on hi/usecase/free-fire-naam-stylish/ and hi/usecase/pubg-bgmi-naam-stylish/, tied to the live name-length checker. This is a case where the site has a real feature and the market has a real complaint in its own words — matching them is free credibility.
phrases.good_example: नाम बहुत लंबा है? चेकर बताता है कि फ्रेम जोड़ने के बाद कितने कैरेक्टर बचे हैं।
phrases.avoid_when: Do not moralise about over-decoration — heavy ornamentation is a deliberate aesthetic in this market, and the site's own product sells it. Frame it as a readability trade-off the user chooses, not a mistake.

phrases.english_concept: domain-wide register observation: this entire vertical borrows English terms wholesale rather than using Sanskritized-Hindi equivalents
phrases.usage_guidance: Confirms current hi/ page titles are already well-calibrated; use as a check against any future copy that drifts toward shuddh/Sanskritized Hindi.
Use over a fully-Sanskritised rendering; Hindi grammar with English technical vocabulary is the natural register

phrases.english_concept: The English head noun Indian users actually search; parallels the Chinese 'blank code' construction
phrases.usage_guidance: Keep the English noun rather than translating it

phrases.english_concept: The paid consumable required to rename in Free Fire
